html:
SMTO-EXE-0140 — That computer has no signed-in desktop for SMTO to use

GUID: 1cc209e6-a213-553a-b3ee-2cdeaa1b64e5
Slug: ui-no-interactive-session
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • SMTO can only work with apps on a desktop that a person is signed in to, and the Gateway on that computer isn't running inside one. SMTO didn't click or type anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the computer running the Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses on that computer), sign in to the desktop and make sure that user's screen is the one being shown. Apps only appear to SMTO inside a desktop that a person is signed in to.
  2. Ask whoever manages that computer to start the Gateway from that signed-in desktop rather than as a background service or over a remote command line. A Gateway started in the background can't see any desktop, even when someone is signed in.
  3. In SMTO, open Settings › Setup › Gateways, select Check connection for that Gateway, then start a new task. SMTO picks up the Gateway's new abilities after this check, and only new tasks use them.

What success looks like

  • Check connection shows that Gateway as connected, and a new task can work with the app.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that computer. A computer with no screen or desktop at all can't run app actions; use a different Gateway for this work.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • UI readiness found no interactive graphical session: no DISPLAY or WAYLAND_DISPLAY on Linux, or no console user session/input desktop on macOS or Windows.

What this means

  • UI readiness found no graphical session environment on Linux or the native desktop reported no usable interactive session on macOS/Windows. Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.

Why this can happen

  • UI readiness found no graphical session environment on Linux or the native desktop reported no usable interactive session on macOS/Windows.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the Gateway process's actual session, especially service/session-zero or headless execution.

How to fix it

  • Run the Gateway inside a logged-in graphical user session on its host: on Linux it needs DISPLAY or WAYLAND_DISPLAY in its environment, on macOS the session must be on the console, and on Windows it must not run as a service in session 0. Headless hosts cannot use native UI; restart the Gateway from the user's desktop session, then refresh its metadata.
  • Run the Gateway in a logged-in graphical user session. Windows services/session 0 and headless hosts cannot interact with native UI.

Retry and execution caution

  • Run the Gateway in a logged-in graphical user session. Windows services/session 0 and headless hosts cannot interact with native UI.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended logged-in session reports native UI availability.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, read secure fields, record input or bypass OS permissions.

Technical notes

  • Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
